context:

Cause found: generated benchmark data has no lifecycle (any session creates it under any run root, nothing removes it), and Time Machine local snapshots kept deleted data allocated. PR #4451 (https://github.com/BenchBox-dev/benchbox/pull/4451) added AGENTS.md [RUN-DATA-001] and made scripts/run_version_matrix.py delete its datagen/ and databases/ when a matrix completes.

description:
Problem: the 2026-11-22 cleanup removed generated data that finished runs still point at.

1. Seven `datagen` symlinks are dangling: `polars-2-1-spill-attribution-20261121/{2.0.0,2.1.0,q4-2.0.0-default,q4-2.1.0-budget4000}/datagen` (target `polars-version-matrix-20261120/datagen`), `polars-version-matrix-reference-20261119/{q41-1.44.2,q41-2.1.0}/datagen` (target that run's own `datagen`), and `duckdb2-followups/bb_2.0.0/datagen` (target `duckdb2-followups/bb_1.5.6/datagen`).
2. 145 result files in `polars-version-matrix-20261120/results` record `working_dir` under `polars-version-matrix-20261120/datagen/...`, which no longer exists. A few results in `dfprim` (12) and `q21-semi` (4) have the same kind of path.
3. `polars-version-matrix-20261120/matrix-manifest.json` pins four SF10 datagen manifest hashes; the data they describe (tpch, tpcds, ssb, clickbench at SF10) was deleted. The hashes were confirmed to match the data before deletion.

4. The same cleanup moved twelve datasets from private run roots into the shared `~/Developer/benchmark_runs/datagen`: `amplab_big_data_sf1`, `coffeeshop_sf00001`, `coffeeshop_sf0001`, `flightdata_sf001`, `nyctaxi_sf01`, `nyctaxi_sf1`, `ssb_sf1` (uncompressed `.tbl`), `tpcds_obt_sf001`, `tpcds_obt_sf01`, `tpcds_obt_sf1`, `tpcds_sf01`, `write_primitives_sf001`. It also replaced `tpchavoc_sf1` with a superset copy from `q21-semi` and added `streams/stream_0.sql` to `tpcds_sf1`. They were generated by package versions 0.5.0rc4 to 0.5.1 under other runs' settings and were not checked against the reuse validation in `benchbox/utils/datagen_version.py`.

Nothing reads the paths in points 1 to 3 today: `scripts/analyze_version_matrix.py` uses the manifest and result files only. The risk is a later rerun or audit that follows a link or path and silently regenerates different data, or concludes evidence was lost.

Expected outcome: each affected folder states plainly that its data was removed and how to regenerate it, and no dangling link remains.
